# What each scan of gate.sh must report (ADR 0062): scan | check | status | requests | result or reason.
# Measured 2026-11-23 with Supabase Auth v2.198.0 on Docker 29.9.3 rootful (3 runs) and rootless Podman 4.9.3 (1 run), cgroup v1,
# linux/amd64, Node 22: the same on every run; the request counts of login and limited re-measured (2 runs, Docker) after a
# wrong login's redirect is followed (ADR 0062 item 4), the results unchanged; login and login2 re-measured with 20 attempts
# (issue #79, ADR 0062 item 7: fewer give no finding) on 2026-11-24, Docker 29.9.3 rootful, cgroup v1 (2 runs).
# The sign-up and reset page scans (ADR 0069, issue #81) measured 2026-11-25 on Docker 29.9.3 rootful, cgroup v1, linux/amd64, Node 22.23.5 (2 runs).
login | login-throttle | ran | 62 | no limit seen in 20 attempts, all answered 303 to /error?code=invalid_credentials; the right password answered 303 to / setting the cookies sb-127-auth-token
login2 | login-throttle | ran | 42 | no limit seen in 20 attempts, all answered 200; the right password answered 303 to / setting the cookies sb-127-auth-token
ignored | login-throttle | failed | 2 | a login with the right password (SIEGEKIT_LOGIN_PASSWORD) and one with a wrong password were both answered 200, so SiegeKit cannot tell that its logins reach the app's login code, and a report of no limit could be false. Check --login-url and --login-body and that SIEGEKIT_LOGIN_PASSWORD is the account's password; a login form that needs JavaScript or a CSRF token needs --login-page
limited | login-throttle | ran | 92 | limited after 30 of 40 attempts: redirected to /error?code=over_request_rate_limit instead of /error?code=invalid_credentials
limited | login-spray | ran | 3 | limited after 1 of 40 attempts: the first login got the answer that showed login-throttle's limit (answered 303 to /error?code=over_request_rate_limit), so the limit holds for other names too
signup-raw | signup-limit | ran | 21 | no limit seen in 20 requests, all answered 200 with no rate-limit header; no answer below 400 differed from the page's own answer to a GET in status, redirect or a new cookie, so SiegeKit cannot tell that its requests reached the app's sign-up code: not reported. Give --mail-catcher to count the emails. A form that only a browser can send (a Next.js Server Action, a CSRF token) needs --signup-page; 20 answered below 400, so up to 20 accounts may have been made, named siegekit-new-...
reset-raw | reset-limit | ran | 21 | no limit seen in 20 requests, all answered 200 with no rate-limit header; no email arrived at the mail catcher http://127.0.0.1:8025/ to the addresses sent: the app sent none for these requests, or does not send its mail there; no answer below 400 differed from the page's own answer to a GET in status, redirect or a new cookie, so SiegeKit cannot tell that its requests reached the app's password-reset code: not reported. A form that only a browser can send (a Next.js Server Action, a CSRF token) needs --reset-page
signup-page | signup-limit | ran | 33 | limit seen after 11 of 20 requests: redirected to /signup?error=too-many-attempts instead of /signup?notice=check-email; 10 emails arrived at the mail catcher http://127.0.0.1:8025/ to the addresses sent for 11 requests answered below 400; 11 answered below 400, so up to 11 accounts may have been made, named siegekit-new-...
